title: My first (usable) walking animation 🥳
author: -Star-Walker-
selftext:
After countless (!) attempts of generating a usable walking animation with LTX2.3 I now used Minimax H3 … and it nailed it first try 😱 There will be some FCPX magic to get rid off the background and some downscaling to production size (it’s 768x1024 right now).   
What would you use, to remove the background? I have some video editing experience, so color keying is my way to go … but maybe, there’s a better solution 🤔

comments.author: AlgaeNo3373
comments.body:
Cute! 

IDK much about it all but I watched a cool corridor crew vid on a new green screen method they cooked up and it's open source, might be worth a look \^\^

replies.author: -Star-Walker-
replies.body: … that’s why I love communities 🤗 Thank you. I’ll have a look.

replies.author: AlgaeNo3373
replies.body:
Yes I think they trained a NN for it iirc which I thought was interesting. IDK if useful though hah. 

What are you making btw? I have racoon-imation on my to-do list myself! \^\^

replies.author: -Star-Walker-
replies.body:
It should become a point and click game engine. I will start with a throwaway proof of concept, just a character walking in a room. Then I will start with the engine itself. To test the engine and see how it performs, I will create a first mini adventure parallel to the engine. It should be a raccoon detective … his case will be „The lost cotton candy“. 

The final product is meant to be a promotion for the books my wife is writing (can’t tell it’s content, but it’s perfect for point and click adventures).

comments.author: sushidrew
comments.body: ive been trying to get mini animal characters to animate well... i am currently using chatgpt to image generate a 3d model, then i use meshy ai for the mesh creation, then i feed that to astra to put into blender and clean up the polygons, but it doesn't do a very good job at animating and creating skeletons. can you explain how you did this? and is it easy to put into godot?

replies.author: -Star-Walker-
replies.body:
It’s actually just a 2d animation. First I created a character in Krea2, then I used Krea2 again to create a character sheet.  


https://preview.redd.it/dt9stapyjbrh1.jpeg?width=2048&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=2970fb2ebd5c254614ddf544ff83ea90240ccd04

  
Then I just used Minimax H3 to animate my little raccoon using reference-to-video. I asked Claude to help me prompting, because prompting for Minimax is a pain in the aaa… afternoon.
